why: The m26 external-arm golden was re-captured on 2026-10-11. This file is the audit trail for that re-capture: what the golden said before, what the live index said, and the proof that the difference was renumbering and not lost data. A re-capture resets the oracle the gate compares against, so it must never be a blank cheque.
indexLastModified: 2026-10-10T23:12 (before this re-capture; not modified by the re-capture)

fingerprintDelta.reading: One internal relationship fewer. Symbols and files identical, external relationships identical.

whyThatIsNotDataLoss.method: The golden stores relationship rowIds, not just counts. Every rowId it references was looked up in the live index. Of 4749 referenced rowIds, 4745 still existed and 4 did not.
whyThatIsNotDataLoss.explanation: All four are internal contains/calls edges in files that grew (parallel-indexer.ts, cli/index.ts). The relationship id embeds the child's line and a per-file sequence ordinal, so re-indexing a grown file RENUMBERS those ids. The edges still exist, with new ordinals:
whyThatIsNotDataLoss.symbolsStillPresent: handleWorkerTimeout, scheduleNext, createWorker, cmdIndex, indexProjectParallel and processWithWorkerPool all still exist in the live index.

postCaptureVerification.method: The re-captured golden was compared against the pre-capture golden edge by edge, normalising away the ordinal and the provenance tag. If the pin had changed behaviour, the edge SET would differ; renumbering alone cannot change membership.

theOneDifference.reading: The same edge. Its id gained an ':m40' provenance tag and the type/name tokens were reordered. Verified present in the live index as type=calls, cmdIndex@46 -> indexProjectParallel@5085. NOT a lost or added relationship.
theOneDifference.note: 648 of 62288 live relationships (1.0%) carry an ':m40' provenance tag. This one is among them.

postCaptureVerification.conclusion: Edge membership is unchanged apart from one edge whose id gained a provenance tag. The walk returns what it returned. The pin changes the plan, not the answer — which is the claim the gate exists to hold.

canary.method: A re-captured oracle is worthless if it cannot fail. One edge was deleted from the re-captured golden and the gate re-run.
canary.result: exit 1, FAIL on the affected root (ast/real-clojure-analyzer.ts:307 analyze). Golden restored byte-identical afterwards and the gate returned to green.
canary.reading: The oracle still detects a one-edge difference. It is a live comparison, not a rubber stamp.

knownStructuralProperty: The golden's 12 roots are drawn from the highest-fan-out symbols in this project, which are in parallel-indexer.ts and cli/index.ts — files that are edited often. So this re-capture will be needed again whenever those files grow. That is a property of the gate, not a one-off, and it is why this file exists rather than a bare commit message.
